title: Project Description
description: Input specification for the Agent Teams build_team pipeline. Describes the project, its deliverables, tools, and components to generate a complete agent team.

project_name.description: Short, slug-safe project name (e.g., 'MyResearchProject', 'DataPipelineV2'). If absent, inferred from the project directory name.

project_goal.description: 1–3 sentence description of what the project produces and why. Used as {PROJECT_GOAL} throughout all agent files.

deliverables.description: List of primary deliverable types this project produces.

output_format.description: The final output format for compiled deliverables (e.g., 'HTML5', 'PDF', 'Python 3.11 modules', 'LaTeX'). Used as {OUTPUT_FORMAT}.

primary_output_dir.description: Directory where primary authored deliverables are written, relative to project root (e.g., 'src/', 'html/chapters/', 'docs/'). Used as {PRIMARY_OUTPUT_DIR}.

build_output_dir.description: Directory where compiled/converted output artifacts go (e.g., 'build/', 'dist/', 'manuscript/'). Used as {BUILD_OUTPUT_DIR}.

figures_dir.description: Directory for diagrams and figures. Used as {FIGURES_DIR}.

existing_project_path.description: Absolute path to an existing project directory on disk. If provided, the analyzer scans it for structure, tools, and potential authority sources.

agents_output_dir.description: Directory where generated agent files will be written. Defaults to '.github/agents/' within the project path.

authority_sources.description: Files or directories that agents must treat as ground truth. Used to build {AUTHORITY_HIERARCHY} and {AUTHORITY_SOURCES_LIST}.

name.description: Human-readable name of this authority source.

path.description: File or directory path, relative to project root or absolute.

scope.description: What types of claims this source is authoritative for.

rank.description: Priority rank in the authority hierarchy (1 = highest).

doc_site_config_file.description: Path to the documentation-site config (e.g. mkdocs.yml). Read by analyze.build_manifest and manifest_format; resolves {DOC_SITE_CONFIG_FILE}. The schema sets additionalProperties:false, so its absence here made every brief declaring this supported key fail validation — including this module's own.

style_reference.description: Path to the style guide, voice samples, or editorial conventions file. Used as {STYLE_REFERENCE_PATH}.

reference_db_path.description: Path to the bibliography or reference database (BibTeX, CSV, JSON, Markdown). Used as {REFERENCE_DB_PATH}.

reference_key_convention.description: Citation key format convention. Used as {REFERENCE_KEY_CONVENTION}.

tools.description: Languages, frameworks, and tools the project uses.

version.description: Version string (e.g., '3.11', '2e', '18'). With version_source, only the generation-time default.

config_files.description: Config files associated with this tool.

needs_specialist_agent.description: If true, generate a dedicated tool-specific agent for this tool.

docs_url.description: Official documentation URL for this tool (e.g., 'https://nodejs.org/docs/latest-v20.x/api/'). May carry '{version}' and '{major_minor}' (the first two version components): without version_source they expand to 'version'; with it, the rendered doc tells the agent to substitute the resolved version. Used as {TOOL_DOCS_URL} in generated agent files.

version_source.description: Where the target project pins this tool's version (e.g., a Lean project's lean/lean-toolchain). When present, generated tool docs do not present 'version' as fixed: they tell the agent to read the pin file, run the resolver when one is given, and consult docs_url for the resolved version. agentteams itself never runs the resolver.

file.description: Pin file path relative to the target project root, without '..' segments (e.g., 'lean/lean-toolchain').

pattern.description: Python regular expression with a named group 'version', applied to the pin file (e.g., 'v(?P<version>[0-9][0-9.]*)').

resolver.description: Optional shell command the agent runs to print the resolved version and documentation URLs (e.g., 'mathagents run lean_docs').

api_surface.description: Key classes, functions, CLI commands, or APIs this tool exposes that agents need to understand. Multi-line Markdown is supported. Used as {TOOL_API_SURFACE} in generated agent files.

common_patterns.description: Common usage patterns, version-specific gotchas, and anti-patterns for this tool. Multi-line Markdown is supported. Used as {TOOL_COMMON_PATTERNS} in generated agent files.

retrieval_integration.description: Structured contract for retrieval query, maintenance, and trigger behavior.

query_entrypoints.description: Files, symbols, or commands where retrieval lookups are executed.

maintenance_entrypoints.description: Commands, scripts, or functions that refresh or rebuild retrieval state.

trigger_sources.description: Trigger channels used to run retrieval workflows.

source_of_truth.description: Tables/files used to verify retrieval correctness and freshness.

staleness_slo_minutes.description: Maximum allowed retrieval staleness window in minutes.

trigger_contract_version.description: Version identifier for retrieval trigger governance.

style_rules.description: Project-specific style rules in plain English. Used in copilot-instructions.md.

pip_package_name.description: PyPI package name for pip distribution (e.g., 'agentteams'). Supplies the package name used by the module-doc-author/validator agents when they are selected, and enables --doc-check / --doc-update flags. Selection of those agents is driven by packaging/docs signals in the project description (pypi, sphinx, mkdocs, readthedocs, sdist).

doc_site_tool.description: Documentation site generator. When set, module-doc-author produces the corresponding config file.

selected_archetypes.description: Override the auto-detected archetype selection. If absent, the analyzer selects archetypes from the project description.

capabilities.description: Explicit, opt-in capabilities this project wants beyond archetype selection. `research_verification` selects the `research-analyst` archetype, which orchestrates the optional `agentteams[research]` runtime library (real, installable Python — not a design-time-only template) — a project must deliberately choose this, since it adds a real runtime dependency to the generated project, unlike every other archetype selection.

privilege_profile.description: Workspace write-confinement posture. DEFAULT IS `confined` as of 2026-W39 (was `cooperative`): sandbox write-confinement is ENABLED BY DEFAULT for every qualifying provider (Claude macOS/Linux; Goose macOS Seatbelt / any framework via the neutral launcher), inert until the operator merges the emitted settings/config example; non-enforcing hosts (Codex, Copilot, native Windows) degrade to the fail-closed advisory, never a silent no-op. Set `cooperative` to opt out: agents are trusted to respect the workspace, no OS boundary emitted (the pre-2026-W39 behavior). `confined` and `exclusive` expand to the `claude:sandbox` host feature, which emits Claude Code's native OS-level sandbox block (write-confines Bash and child processes to workspace_write_roots) into the settings example the operator merges — inert until merged. `exclusive` adds OS read-exclusion on top of `confined` (P3a): it also denies this team reading a default deny set plus any `protected_read_paths`, and prints a P3b inbound-hardening advisory. This is OUTBOUND (it seals this team's reads); keeping OTHER teams out of this workspace is operator filesystem hardening, not something exclusive enforces. The effective feature set is the UNION of this expansion and any --target-host-features tokens, so cooperative never strips an explicitly-requested claude:sandbox token. Only the Claude framework enforces this today; on non-sandbox hosts (Goose, Codex, Copilot, native Windows) selecting confined/exclusive emits an advisory notice, not enforcement.

goose_egress_proxy.description: Sanctioned single egress endpoint for an `exclusive` (network-isolated) goose team, as `host[:port]`. Apple Seatbelt's `remote ip` accepts ONLY `localhost` or `*` as the host (an IP/DNS literal makes sandbox-exec refuse to load the whole profile), so this must be a LOOPBACK proxy — e.g. `localhost:8888` for the goose route-proxy. Only meaningful with privilege_profile: exclusive on a goose (macOS) target; the default `confined` profile leaves egress open. HONEST RESIDUAL: the endpoint is a bidirectional channel; agentteams cannot close exfiltration through it.

workspace_write_roots.description: Directories the confined agent may write to, relative to the merged .claude/settings.json at the project root. Only meaningful when privilege_profile is confined/exclusive (or claude:sandbox is selected directly). Defaults to ["."] — the whole generated project tree is the workspace. Validated at generation (fail-closed): '/', '~', $HOME and their ancestors, the signing-key directory, home credential/persistence paths, the project control plane (.git, .claude, .goose, .codex, .github/agents, .github/hooks, sandbox, .agentteams) and shell/glob metacharacters are refused. A NEW root outside the project (absolute, ~/..., ../...) needs the operator's --accept-write-root PATH unless the live .claude/settings.json allowWrite already holds it. This file is agent-writable data; generation prints every added root with its source.

write_policy.description: Orchestrator-only-writes pilot (opt-in). "orchestrator-only": non-orchestrator agents are narrowed to read-only tools and return typed change/deletion proposals and command requests carrying a dispatch nonce. The orchestrator queues them for the out-of-session runner (agentteams --serve-requests, started by the operator outside every agent session), which alone holds the ledger key (a 0600 file in ~/.config/agentteams/keys) and applies them under the policy below, running commands and gates in an OS sandbox (confined_programs). Turns on the AR_WRITE_POLICY audit check and forces goose_tool_scoping "grant". Allowed only on claude and goose, with privilege_profile not "cooperative" (their session sandbox keeps the key file from the orchestrator); generation refuses it elsewhere.

mcp_catalog.description: MCP catalogue opt-ins (agentteams/templates/mcp/). The first-party read-only servers agentteams-recall and agentteams-gitread are on by default wherever an MCP host-feature token is set; list them here only to opt in on Codex (which ignores scope). github-read, github-write and fetch are opt-in templates, emitted inert with their security metadata until the operator activates them. Each server is scoped to its role scope intersected with the roster. Under write_policy orchestrator-only nothing from the catalogue is emitted (the GitHub servers wait for P5). A GitHub id also brings in the pr-manager and pr-notifier agents.

mcp_catalog_exclude.description: MCP catalogue ids to leave out, including the default-on ones.

pr_management.description: Add the pr-manager and pr-notifier agents (pull-request lifecycle and reviewer notification). Also implied by opting into github-read or github-write in mcp_catalog. Default false.

write_policy_frameworks.description: Orchestrator-only-writes pilot (P5a): the frameworks the switch covers when one brief emits several. Each listed framework renders under write_policy; every other framework renders as if the switch were off and is outside the pilot's guarantee. Unset: the switch applies to the framework being generated and is refused off claude/goose.

agent_policies.description: Per-agent policy for --apply-proposal / --run-request. write_scopes: files, directories ending in '/', or patterns (P5b: '*', '?' and '[...]' match within one segment and never match a dot-segment (a trailing '/' covers everything below, dot-files included), e.g. 'reports/dossiers/*/strategy.md'; the first segment literal; no '**', '..' or control plane) the agent may change via proposals (never the brief itself). commands: allowed command requests, each an exact argv prefix plus one regex per remaining argument (fullmatch; patterns admitting options or parent/absolute paths are refused), with an optional pinned cwd, variadic last pattern, owned writes and stdin gates.

cwd.description: Pinned working directory (project-relative, default "."); a request must use exactly this.

variadic.description: When true, the last argument pattern matches one or more trailing arguments.

writes.description: Globs this command may change (e.g. a protected record its script owns); expected_writes outside them must be in the agent's write_scopes.

stdin_gates.description: Gates run on stdin_from_content before it is piped; without this key, stdin content is refused.

timeout.description: Seconds before the command is killed (P5a; default 600).

proposal_gates.description: Pre-write gates run on the proposed content: {name: {glob, argv, exec?}}. glob is fnmatch on the lowercased path, so '*' crosses '/' (unlike a write_scopes pattern, where '*' matches one segment). exec (P4b): the programs the gate may run inside the runner's sandbox (default: its own program and a shebang interpreter). P5c: set it in the operator-owned confined file's reserved gate_exec key instead, to keep machine paths out of the committed brief; setting both is refused. In argv, {file} (a temporary copy of the proposed content) and {path} (the destination, context only) must be whole arguments; shells are refused. A non-zero exit refuses the proposal.

confined_programs.description: Orchestrator-only-writes pilot (P4b): per-agent OS sandbox for the commands the out-of-session runner runs for that agent: {agent: {exec, write}}. exec: absolute or ~/ paths (programs or toolchain roots, matched as subpaths; macOS only, decision C) the command may execute. write: project-relative directories it may write (never the project root, .agentteams, .agentteams-queue, .git or the control plane; never containing an exec path). Changes inside write roots count as declared. An agent without an entry gets no --run-request. P5b: prefer the operator-owned file ~/.config/agentteams/confined/<project>-<hash>.json (agentteams --confined-path / --install-confined), which keeps machine paths out of the committed brief; the runner reads it instead of this block and refuses when both are set.

allow_unconfined_runs.description: Orchestrator-only-writes pilot (P4b, decision A): let the runner run commands and gates unconfined when no OS sandbox is usable. Off by default (refuse); every unconfined run is logged in the ledger.

protected_paths.description: Globs no proposal may touch (records changed only through their own scripts); a pattern without wildcards also covers everything below it. The project control plane and the brief are always refused as well.

goose_tool_scoping.description: How Goose recipes get their extensions. "legacy" (default): every recipe loads the whole developer builtin (shell + file writes). "grant": each recipe's extensions are derived from the agent's declared tools — read/search -> the read-only agentteams_readfs stdio server (scripts/goose-readfs-mcp.py, or .agentteams/bin/goose-readfs-mcp.py under write_policy orchestrator-only; launched python3 -I -S; shipped only in this mode); edit -> developer [write, edit, tree]; execute -> developer [shell, tree]; agent -> summon [delegate, load]. Any recipe with developer turns off Goose's auto-added analyze extension. A read-only agent gets no developer at all. Merges keep a recipe's on-disk extensions, so switching an existing team to grant needs a full re-render (--update --overwrite).

coordination_write_roots.description: Sibling/adjacent-repo write roots this team coordinates into (cross-repo file-based coordination). Unioned into workspace_write_roots at generation (same merge point as capability grants) so every sandbox emitter — Claude allowWrite, Goose Seatbelt, and the Linux confine-run.sh launcher — sees them. On Linux these become `--coord-root` binds that FAIL CLOSED (never silently create the dir) when the declared sibling path is missing, so a misconfigured sibling surfaces as a clear error instead of a bwrap init crash. A declared coordination root is operator config and is weaker than an authenticated capability grant; both feed the same union. Presence of this field also signals a team that needs the coordination MCP surface. Validated at generation (fail-closed): '/', '~', $HOME and their ancestors, the signing-key directory, home credential/persistence paths, the project control plane (.git, .claude, .goose, .codex, .github/agents, .github/hooks, sandbox, .agentteams) and shell/glob metacharacters are refused. A NEW root outside the project (absolute, ~/..., ../...) needs the operator's --accept-write-root PATH unless the live .claude/settings.json allowWrite already holds it. This file is agent-writable data; generation prints every added root with its source.

team_id.description: Stable identity this workspace/team is known by for cross-workspace capability grants (P2). A grant is issued BY one team_id and held BY another; the holder's generation-time sandbox-widening reads grants where holder_team == this id. Defaults to the slugified project_name when absent. IMPORTANT: the id is operator-assigned and must be UNIQUE across your workspaces — two teams sharing a team_id share each other's granted reach. Under the symmetric-key model the holder identity is a name (not key-authenticated); it is safe only because grants are consumed at operator-run generation time, never at agent runtime.

protected_read_paths.description: P3a read-exclusion: extra paths the `exclusive` privilege_profile OS-denies this team (and its subprocesses) from reading, on top of a curated default deny set of sensitive dotfile locations. Add sibling-workspace roots here to stop THIS team reading them. Only meaningful with privilege_profile: exclusive. This is OUTBOUND hardening (it seals this team's reads); it does NOT stop other teams from reading THIS workspace, which is operator filesystem hardening (see the exclusive-profile advisory printed at generation and the docs). Paths use the sandbox syntax (home-relative or absolute).

resolve_deny_read_abspath.description: P3-3 opt-in (default false). When true, the `exclusive` profile's `~/`-relative `denyRead` paths are resolved to `expanduser`'d ABSOLUTE paths at generation time, so OS read-exclusion no longer depends on Claude Code expanding `~`→$HOME before the deny (an unverified assumption that, if false, silently no-ops every default deny entry while the config still looks protective). Trade-off: absolute paths are host-specific (they name the generating machine's home) and do not port to another machine — regenerate on the host that runs the team. Only meaningful with privilege_profile: exclusive; the default (false) keeps the portable `~/` form and a byte-identical block.

protect_prompt_roots.description: Follow-up #8 phase 2 opt-in (default false). When true and a sandbox is emitted, the Claude block adds permissions.deny Edit(...) rules for the prompt roots other harnesses read as instructions (.github/copilot-instructions.md, .github/instructions/, .github/prompts/, .github/agents/, AGENTS.md, .goosehints, .codex/, .goose/recipes/, CLAUDE.md, CLAUDE.local.md, .mcp.json, and .agentteams/ when present) plus sandbox denyWrite entries for those present at generation; the Linux goose runner example passes confine-run.sh --protect-prompt-roots (read-only binds of the present roots). .github/workflows is NOT covered and the goose macOS Seatbelt profile is unchanged (deferred). Off by default because it also blocks sandboxed agents (and an in-sandbox agentteams --update) from authoring Copilot, Codex and goose agents and instructions. Turning it off prints a SANDBOX RELAXATION notice when the live .claude/settings.json still carries the rules.

framework_conformance_check.description: Opt-in override for the framework-watch reference's ≤24h standard-conformance-check section (see references/provider-adapter-refresh.procedure.md §7). When omitted, defaults on for teams that maintain framework adapters (a component with slug `framework-adapters`, i.e. the `@framework-adapters-expert` role) and off otherwise. Set true to force-emit the section (e.g. the AgentTeamsModule self-brief dogfooding the trigger onto its own governing team) or false to suppress it. The check itself is read-only detection + routing (Constitutional C-4); it never edits adapter code.

enforce_decision_signing.description: Strict agent-privilege switch (agent-position axis). When true, an AUTHORIZING security-decision row (a PASS or HALT-RETRACTED that clears a destructive/privileged action) is honoured ONLY if decision signing is active and the row's signature verifies; an unsigned authorization is refused (fail-closed) rather than trusted on its author name alone — closing the roster/author-spoof path in the signing-inactive configuration. Emitted into the generated team as references/agent-privilege.json, which the security gate reads at enforcement time. DEFAULTS ON when the team is (re)generated or updated: a post-update notice names how to turn it off (set this field false in your brief and re-update). A workspace with NO emitted config is treated as OFF, so a team that has not yet been updated to this feature never breaks by surprise — the switch turns on precisely when you update. Set false to keep the legacy behavior (an unsigned authorizing row is honoured on its author name).

is_management_repo.description: Endow this repository as a MANAGEMENT repository (default false). When true, the team is designated a manager: its orchestrator may ISSUE signed management directives (`agentteams --issue-directive`) that relay the operator's direction to agents in the operator's other (managed) repos. A management directive is an authenticated operator artifact — signed with the operator-provisioned AGENTTEAMS_MANAGEMENT_SIGNING_KEY — that lets a managed agent proceed on the EXACT non-destructive task it names without re-asking the operator for approval. It can NEVER clear C-5 destruction, pierce a C-2 HALT, or change governance (such scopes are auto-refused). Being a manager does not change what the team's own agents may do; it only enables issuing directives. Same-trust-domain model: the operator controls the key and all repos; symmetric HMAC defeats keyless injection, not a key-holder (the same trust boundary as capability grants / signed waivers). Set false (default) and nothing changes.

authorized_managers.description: Team-ids of the MANAGEMENT repositories this (managed) team accepts signed directives from (default empty — accepts none, the current behavior). Emitted as references/authorized-managers.txt (the roster) plus references/management-authority.json. A directive is honoured only if its manager_team is on this roster AND its signature verifies against AGENTTEAMS_MANAGEMENT_SIGNING_KEY AND it is unexpired/unexhausted AND its task_scope is an exact, non-destructive, non-governance scope (destructive/bulk/cross-repo and constitution/Invariant-Core/reference-template/grant/roster/key/enforcement scopes are mechanically refused regardless of a valid signature). An empty roster or a non-verifying directive is inert (the agent asks the operator as today). Enrolling a manager here is a privileged cross-repo change requiring @security clearance.

components.description: Workstream components. One workstream expert agent is generated per component.

name.description: Human-readable name of this component (e.g., 'Chapter 1: Introduction').

output_file.description: Path to this component's primary output file, relative to primary_output_dir.

description.description: 1–3 sentences describing what this component produces.

sections.description: List of sections, functions, or sub-units in this component.

sources.description: Known source references (citation keys or file paths) relevant to this component.

cross_refs.description: Other component slugs this component references.

quality_criteria.description: Pass/fail quality criteria the workstream expert will check against in reviews.

tools.description: Tool or agent slugs relevant to this component (e.g., 'PostgreSQL', 'Docker'). Used to link workstream experts to tool specialists/references.

memory_index_extra_dirs.description: Optional consumer-declared extra source directories or glob patterns merged into the durable memory index in addition to the built-in defaults (workSummaries/, docs_src/, references/, CHANGELOG.md, README.md). Each entry is a project-relative string: a directory (recursively scanned for *.md) or a glob (literal expansion). Absolute paths, traversal escapes, and symlinked escapes outside the project root are rejected. See docs_src/api-reference/memory-index.md.

memory_index_exclude.description: Optional consumer-declared project-relative paths/globs to EXCLUDE from the durable memory index, even when they would otherwise be swept in by the built-in defaults (workSummaries/, docs_src/, references/) or by memory_index_extra_dirs. Each entry is matched against a source's project-relative posix path as a directory prefix (entry, or entry + '/') or an fnmatch glob. Use this when durable content has been relocated out of the repository (e.g. to a private work-docs repo) so its paths and content snippets are not embedded in the committed, publicly-visible index. Absolute paths are ignored. See docs_src/api-reference/memory-index.md.

code_index_extra_dirs.description: Optional consumer-declared extra directories or glob patterns of local scripts merged into the code & API index's local-script partition, in addition to the git-tracked source files discovered by default. Each entry is a project-relative string: a directory (recursively scanned for *.py/*.sh) or a glob (literal expansion of *.py/*.sh). Absolute paths, traversal escapes, and symlinked escapes outside the project root are rejected. The code index is a gitignored local cache. See docs_src/api-reference/code-index.md.

conversion_pipeline.description: Command or tool used to convert primary deliverables to output format. Used as {CONVERSION_PIPELINE} in format-converter agent.

mcp_hints.description: Optional consumer-declared hints about external integrations that may warrant an MCP server. Each entry feeds the MCP-suitability detection rubric (agentteams.mcp_detect). Purely advisory: the rubric only recommends; it never auto-provisions a credentialed server. See references/mcp-auto-detection-report.md §5.

integration.description: Name of the external system or capability (e.g., 'analytics-warehouse', 'jira').

stateful.description: True if the integration has an auth/session lifecycle, connection pooling, or caching that materially benefits from a persistent server.

used_by_components.description: Component slugs that need this integration. Reuse across >=2 components is a positive signal.

trust_tier.description: Self-declared trust level (REQUIRED so absence cannot silently default to the permissive case). Any third-party-* value routes the candidate to DEFER_TO_SECURITY_REVIEW.

max_side_effect.description: Most-privileged operation the integration needs. 'destructive' routes the candidate to DEFER_TO_SECURITY_REVIEW.

large_dynamic_surface.description: True if the operation set is large and changes over time. Only a positive signal when commits_lazy_disclosure is also true; otherwise an efficiency anti-pattern (report §4.1).

commits_lazy_disclosure.description: True if the integration commits to lazy/progressive tool disclosure. Required for large_dynamic_surface to count as a positive signal (report §5.1 tiebreaker).

mcp_servers.description: Optional operator-SPECIFIED MCP server definitions to emit for this team (each conforms to mcp-server.schema.json). This is the input for automating *specified* servers (vs. mcp_hints, which only feeds the BUILD/USE/DEFER detection rubric). Purely declarative: entries are copied to the team-manifest's mcp_servers[] and emitted as the INERT .claude/mcp-servers.agentteams.json only when an MCP host-feature token is enabled (claude:mcp or bridge:copilot-vscode-to-claude:mcp). Provisions nothing on its own; credentialed activation remains a separate operator step. See references/mcp-auto-detection-report.md §5.4/§6.

recipe_parameters.description: Optional Goose recipe parameters (Phase-4a goose-native). Declares typed runtime inputs for the generated Goose team: copied to the team-manifest and, for --framework goose, emitted as a `parameters:` block on the ORCHESTRATOR recipe (referenced via {{ key }}) so it accepts `goose run --recipe orchestrator.yaml --params key=value`. Goose-only; ignored by other frameworks. Opt-in: absent/empty → recipes byte-identical.

requirement.description: Goose requirement (default: optional). Optional non-file params receive a default; file params are coerced to required (goose forbids file defaults).

default.description: Default for optional non-file params (file params cannot have a default).

recipe_response.description: Optional Goose recipe response schema (Phase-4b goose-native). A JSON Schema ({type:object, properties, required, ...}) declaring the team's structured output; for --framework goose it is copied to the team-manifest and emitted as a `response:` block (json_schema) on the ORCHESTRATOR recipe so goose validates the final output against it. Goose-only; ignored by other frameworks. Opt-in: absent → recipes byte-identical.

recipe_retry.description: Optional Goose recipe retry config (Phase-4c goose-native). Declares self-validation for the generated Goose team: for --framework goose it is copied to the team-manifest and emitted as a `retry:` block on the ORCHESTRATOR recipe so goose re-runs until the shell `checks` pass. Safety: `max_retries` is clamped to 1-10 (default 3) and a bounded `timeout_seconds` (1-3600, default 300) is always emitted (never an unbounded retry). Requires ≥1 valid check or it is dropped. Goose-only; ignored by other frameworks. Opt-in: absent → recipes byte-identical.

timeout_seconds.description: Per-check command timeout in seconds (clamped to 1-3600; default 300).

checks.description: Shell checks defining success; ALL must pass.

command.description: Shell command; non-zero exit = check failed.

on_failure.description: Shell command run when checks fail (optional).
